You are Aura — a general-purpose AI agent that works
on the user's machine: run commands, read and write files, crawl a given
website, and help with whatever they ask. You are talking with a human in an
interactive session. Rules:
- Answer directly and conversationally first — short, natural, human.
  Greetings get greetings; questions get answers.
- Prove what you claim: record results about the user's work (a bug
  fixed, a feature working, tests passing) with finding_add, right after
  the reads or test run that show it — not answers, recollections or
  plans. Aura re-runs them; if it says "not proven", try once more at
  most, then say so in your answer; only proven results enter the report.
- Stay inside scope; Aura enforces it and refuses anything outside.
- Prefer evidence over guessing; validate before claiming success.
- If a fact you need isn't given and you can't find it, say it's missing
  instead of filling it in.
- Your body has organs — declared here, like your tools, so you never have
  to rediscover them. Pblock judgment layer: src/agent_core/pblock_engine
  (persona seats with lived stores, ground compiler, judge heads). When a
  task needs trained judgment, train and use YOUR organ
  (agent_core.pblock_engine.train_pblock) — do not build a replacement.
- When the objective is achieved, reply with a concise final report.

Planning discipline: for any multi-step task, FIRST call
todo_write with one pending item per step, then work through them — set
in_progress when starting an item, done when it's finished. The operator sees
the checklist live, and it is shown to you every step.
Read TASK.md in this directory and do the task.

Only untagged user messages are the user's own words; each starts with when it arrived [day date time] — don't write such stamps yourself.]

content:
1:b2|# TASK
2:dc|The project (learn, checked out at an old commit) has this issue:
3:00|
4:37|LassoLarsIC: unintuitive copy_X behaviour
5:a2|Hi, I would like to report what seems to be a bug in the treatment of the `copy_X` parameter of the `LassoLarsIC` class. Because it's a simple bug, it's much easier to see in the code directly than in the execution, so I am not posting steps to reproduce it.
6:00|
7:3e|As you can see here, LassoLarsIC accepts a copy_X parameter.
8:a8|https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/7389dbac82d362f296dc2746f10e43ffa1615660/sklearn/linear_model/least_angle.py#L1487
9:00|
10:68|However, it also takes a copy_X parameter a few lines below, in the definition of ```fit```.
11:3d|    ```def fit(self, X, y, copy_X=True):```
12:00|
13:3b|Now there are two values (potentially contradicting each other) for copy_X and each one is used once. Therefore ```fit``` can have a mixed behaviour. Even worse, this can be completely invisible to the user, since copy_X has a default value of True. Let's assume that I'd like it to be False, and have set it to False in the initialization, `my_lasso = LassoLarsIC(copy_X=False)`. I then call ```my_lasso.fit(X, y)``` and my choice will be silently overwritten. 
14:00|
15:2a|Ideally I think that copy_X should be removed as an argument in ```fit```. No other estimator seems to have a duplication in class parameters and fit arguments (I've checked more than ten in the linear models module). However, this would break existing code. Therefore I propose that ```fit``` takes a default value of `None` and only overwrites the existing value if the user has explicitly passed it as an argument to ```fit```. I will submit a PR to that effect.
16:00|
17:00|
18:ab|Find the cause and make the minimal correct fix in the source (not in tests).
19:07|Do NOT modify or add tests. Do NOT commit. Leave your changes in the working tree.

content: The bug is clear: `LassoLarsIC.fit` has its own `copy_X=True` parameter that shadows the constructor's `self.copy_X` — the fit arg is passed to `lars_path` while `self.copy_X` goes to `_preprocess_data`, so a `copy_X=False` set at init is silently ignored. Let me check the tests to confirm the expected behavior before fixing.
reasoning_content:
The bug: `fit(self, X, y, copy_X=True)` — the `copy_X` param in fit shadows the constructor's `self.copy_X`. In `fit`, `self.copy_X` is used for `_preprocess_data`, but `copy_X` (the fit arg) is used for `lars_path`. The fix per the issue: `fit` takes default `None` and only overwrites if explicitly passed.

The actual upstream fix (scikit-learn PR #9345) was:

```python
def fit(self, X, y, copy_X=None):

    X, y = check_X_y(X, y, y_numeric=True)

    max_iter = self.max_iter

    Gram = self.precompute

    copy_X = self.copy_X if copy_X is None else copy_X
    ...
```

- docstring updated to document the `None` fallback
